description: Đá cây: a five-kilo chunk sawn off a metre-long block of ice from the ice depot, where the blocks are frozen in steel moulds and hauled out at dawn on a ba gác under wet jute sacks.  It is meant for chilling fish and beer crates, not for your glass: the depot freezes whatever comes out of its well.  In this heat it melts into a puddle of untreated water in about ten hours, and nothing, not even a styrofoam box, will stop it.
//: Melts by countdown: 5 kg of ice -> 20 x 250 ml of untreated water.  The engine's countdown ignores pocket insulation, so a thùng xốp does not slow it.

description: Đá viên: a two-kilo plastic bag of hollow ice tubes from a factory that freezes filtered water, the clean ice that cafés buy for drinks.  It sweats through the bag as you carry it, and in about four hours it is a bag of cold, clean water.
//: Melts by countdown: 2 kg of clean ice -> 8 x 250 ml of clean water.

description: Đá bào: a cup of ice shaved off a block on a hand-cranked plane, or knocked out of a bag of tube ice and cracked with a pestle, to go under chè, into iced coffee or over a glass of tea.  It lasts less than an hour in the open.
